idea.body: Absolute value only cares how far a number is from zero, not which direction. |-5| and |5| both equal 5, since -5 and 5 each sit 5 steps from zero. That is why |x| = 5 has two solutions, x = 5 and x = -5. Both are 5 steps from zero, just on opposite sides. To solve |x - 3| = 5, think of x as being 5 steps from 3 instead of from zero. That gives x = 8 or x = -2. An absolute value inequality works the same way. |x| < 5 means every point closer to zero than 5 steps, and |x| > 5 means every point farther away than that.

figure.alt: A number line from -6 to 6: both -5 and 5 sit 5 steps from zero.

steps: |x - 3| = 5 means x is 5 steps from 3, in either direction.
Going up from 3: x - 3 = 5, so x = 8.
Going down from 3: x - 3 = -5, so x = -2.
Both 8 and -2 are 5 steps from 3, so both are solutions.

figure.alt: A number line centered at 3: the solutions -2 and 8 both sit 5 steps from 3.

stretch.prompt: The equation |x - 2| = k has exactly one solution for exactly one value of k. What is that value of k?
explanation: Any positive k gives two solutions, one on each side of 2.
Any negative k gives no solution at all.
Only k = 0 gives exactly one solution, x = 2.
stretch.useAgain: when thinking about how many solutions an absolute value equation has, not just what they are.
hints: Try a positive value of k and count the solutions, then try a negative one.
One value of k gives neither two solutions nor none.
stretch.socraticHint: What happens to the number of solutions as k shrinks toward zero?
